slides.1.title: The Ruby Family: From Basic to Top Quality
slides.1.html:
🍓 Ruby (basic)

  • Aged 2–3 years in large oak vats, keeping a deep ruby colour and fresh fruit aromas
  • Blackberry, blueberry and blackcurrant fruit, clearly sweet, 19–20% alcohol
  • Ready to drink immediately, no ageing needed, generally non-vintage

🏅 Ruby Reserve (Reserva)

  • Higher quality than basic Ruby: selected grapes and longer cask ageing (usually 3–4 years)
  • Major houses have their own brand names, such as Graham's Six Grapes, Dow's Trademark and Ramos Pinto Adriano
  • More complex, with chocolate, spice and dark fruit

🍷 Crusted Port

  • An unfiltered blend of several vintages of red Port, aged in bottle for at least 3 years, forming a deposit (crust)
  • Needs decanting; sits between LBV and Vintage, with good value
  • Uncommon today, with the tradition kept up mainly by houses such as Churchill's
slides.2.title: LBV vs. Single Quinta vs. Vintage: The Top Ruby Styles
slides.2.html:
🍷 LBV (Late Bottled Vintage) — two versions!

  • Filtered LBV: aged 4–6 years in cask, then filtered and bottled. Ready to drink, no sediment, lower price. Produced in volume with consistent quality
  • Unfiltered LBV: ⭐ aged 4–6 years in cask, then bottled without filtration. Needs decanting, keeps more sediment and is more complex. Examples: LBVs from Graham's・Ramos Pinto・Niepoort

🌟 Single Quinta Vintage

  • Made in a good year that is not declared, from the single best Quinta
  • Bottled after 2 years in cask, and needs long bottle ageing (10–20 years)
  • Often better value than official Vintage Port: comparable quality at a lower price
  • Examples: Quinta do Vesúvio (Symington), Quinta do Crasto, Quinta do Vale Meão

🥇 Vintage Port (top)

  • Made only in the best years officially declared (roughly every 3–4 years)
  • Bottled after 2 years in cask, then aged 20–50 years in bottle
  • The highest quality, the highest price and the longest ageing potential
  • Top vintages: 2011・2007・2000・1994・1985・1977
slides.3.title: The Ruby Styles from Lowest to Highest: Full Comparison
slides.3.items.0.desc: Non-vintage, aged about 2–3 years in large vats, deep red fruit, ready to drink, the most basic Port
slides.3.items.1.label: LBV (filtered)
slides.3.items.1.desc: Single vintage, 4–6 years in cask, ready to drink, mass-produced, vintage Port at good value
slides.3.items.2.label: LBV (unfiltered)
slides.3.items.2.desc: Single vintage, 4–6 years in cask, needs decanting, markedly greater complexity, a true tasting experience
slides.3.items.3.desc: The very top: 2 years in cask + 20–50 years in bottle; every bottle is a unique journey through time
slides.4.question: What is the main difference between "unfiltered" and "filtered" LBV (Late Bottled Vintage)?
slides.4.options.0: Unfiltered is aged for less time, filtered for longer
slides.4.options.1: Unfiltered keeps sediment, is more complex and needs decanting; filtered is ready to drink with no sediment
slides.4.options.2: Unfiltered uses only Touriga Nacional, filtered uses a blend of varieties
slides.4.options.3: Unfiltered is made only in top vintages
slides.4.explanation: This is the most commonly confused point about LBV. Filtered LBV is filtered clear before bottling, is ready to drink, has no sediment and is made in volume. Unfiltered LBV keeps its natural sediment, needs decanting and is more complex. It usually comes from well-known producers and is the LBV truly worth collecting.
slides.5.question: Under what circumstances is Single Quinta Vintage Port usually made?
slides.5.options.0: Every year, from the best single estate
slides.5.options.1: In a good year not declared as an official Vintage, from the single best Quinta
slides.5.options.2: Only in the very best years, alongside the official Vintage
slides.5.options.3: A special style produced jointly by several estates
slides.5.explanation: Single Quinta Vintage is usually made in a "second-best" year that has not been declared an official Vintage Port, from the single best Quinta (estate). These wines often offer better value than official Vintage: comparable quality at a lower price, and a favourite of connoisseurs.
